title: Derivative of the Gaussian mean score
statement: For any real numbers $c,z$ and any nonnegative variance $v$, the function $m\mapsto \frac{z-m}{v}p_v(m,z)$ has derivative at $m=c$ equal to $\left(\frac{(z-c)^2}{v^2}-\frac1v\right)p_v(c,z)$, where $p_v$ is the Gaussian density with mean $m$ and variance $v$ (with the zero-variance density taken to be zero).
replaced: For $v\ge0$, put $p_v(c,z)=(2\pi v)^{-1/2}\exp(-(z-c)^2/(2v))$ when $v>0$, and $p_0(c,z)=0$; take division by zero to be zero. For real $c,z$, the derivative at $c$ of $m\mapsto((z-m)/v)p_v(m,z)$ is $((z-c)^2/v^2-1/v)p_v(c,z)$.
